questions.q: Which of the following animals was not known to the people of the Indus Valley Civilization?
questions.question_type: Negative/Exception MCQ — Single Correct
questions.explanation: Among the given options, the people of the Indus Valley Civilization were familiar with the bull and the elephant, but scholars differ regarding the presence of the horse. It is difficult to determine with certainty whether the bones obtained from various Harappan sites belong to the wild ass/ onager (Equus hemionus khur) or to the domesticated horse (Equus caballus). Evidence of the horse, or other animals of the same group, has been reported from Rangpur, Rana Ghundai, Lothal, Surkotada, Kuntasi and Kalibangan. A scholar reported that among the so-called horse remains found from Surkotada, six were genuine horse remains dating to around 2000 BCE, i. e., around the middle of the last part of the third millennium BCE. In 1974, J. P. Joshi and A. K. Sharma of the Archaeological Survey of India reported that horse bones were found at every level here between 2100– 1700 BCE. However, Ramsharan Sharma, Romila Thapar, Mando, etc., do not accept this. Similarly, the teeth claimed to be of a horse by Brigadier E. J. Ross from the Early Harappan site of Rana Ghundai are considered inauthentic by Zauner. Therefore, regarding the horse, it would be appropriate to say that its presence in the Harappan Civilization cannot be completely denied, though its use must have been extremely limited. The Bihar Public Service Commission accepted option (b) as the answer.

questions.q: When did the use of iron begin in the Indian subcontinent?

questions.explanation: There are differences of opinion among scholars about the beginning of iron use in the Indian subcontinent. Some scholars believe that the Hittites were the first in the world to begin using iron, and only after that did its use spread to other countries. However, excavations at the Ban Chiang archaeological site in Thailand have yielded cast iron, dated approximately to 1600–1200 BCE. In India, iron has been found from the Doab area of Noh (Rajasthan) along with Black-and-Red Ware, and its probable date is considered around 1400 BCE. The earliest clear references to this metal are found in texts of the Later Vedic period (about 1000–600 BCE.). In the Atharvaveda, iron is mentioned as “Shyama Ayas” (dark metal), and there is also a reference to an iron ploughshare. Excavations at Atranjikhera (Uttar Pradesh) have yielded the earliest agricultural iron tools along with remains of wheat, barley, and rice. Archaeologists have dated it to around 1000 BCE., which is accepted by most scholars.

questions.q: Gautama Buddha was elevated to the position of God during the period of:
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: In the reign of Kanishka, at the Fourth Buddhist Council, Buddhism got clearly divided into two distinct and independent sects—Hinayana and Mahayana. In the Mahayana branch, Buddha was regarded as a deity and began to be worshipped. Along with this, the worship of many Bodhisattvas also started.

questions.q: The teachers from whom Buddha first attempted to gain enlightenment after the Mahabhinishkramana were:
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: After the Mahabhinishkramana, in search of knowledge, Lord Buddha reached the hermitage of Alara Kalama and took initiation from him. He practised austerities there, but he was not satisfied. Alara Kalama was a teacher of Sankhya philosophy and was famous for his spiritual powers; therefore, Buddha first attempted to gain knowledge from Alara Kalama and Rudraka Ramaputra.

questions.q: Which one of the following is not common between Buddhism and Jainism?
questions.question_type: Negative/Exception MCQ — Single Correct
questions.explanation: Avoidance of extremes of self-mortification (tapas) and sensual indulgence, and the adoption of the Middle Path, is followed only in Buddhism, not in Jainism. However, disbelief in the authority of the Vedas, denial of the efficacy of rituals, and prohibition of violence against living beings are found in both religions.

questions.q: Nalanda University was a great center of knowledge of -
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: Nalanda University was world-famous for the study of Buddhist philosophy. Around the middle of the fifth century A. D., during the Gupta period, Nalanda came into existence. Kumaragupta I first donated to the Nalanda Buddhist monastery, and later Gupta rulers such as Buddhagupta, Tathagatagupta, and Baladitya also made donations to the monastery.

questions.q: Where was Mahavira Swami born?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: Mahavira Swami was born at Kundagrama or Kundalpur (near Vaishali) around 599 B. C. His mother Trishala was the sister of Chetaka, the chief of the Licchavi republican state of Vaishali, and his father Siddhartha was the head of the confederation of the Jnatrika Kshatriyas. His elder brother was Nandivardhana. In some old editions of National Council of Educational Research and Training books, Mahavira’s birth year is mentioned as 540 B. C. On this basis, many other publishers also printed the same year in their books, creating confusion. The correct birth year of Mahavira is 599 B. C., because Mahavira belonged to a period earlier than Gautama Buddha. Gautama Buddha was born in 563 B. C. In the newer editions of National Council of Educational Research and Training, Mahavira’s birth year is now published as 599 B. C.

questions.q: The first disciple of Lord Mahavira was –
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: Lord Mahavira was born in 599 B. C. to Siddhartha, a feudatory of the Kshatriya lineage. His wife’s name was Yashoda, and they had a daughter named Priyadarshana. That daughter was married to Jamali, who later became a follower of Mahavira Swami. He was Mahavira’s first disciple.

questions.q: The salvation place of Mahavira, the Propounder of Jain religion, is located at -:

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The place of salvation (nirvana) of Mahavira Swami—the real propounder of Jainism or the 24th Tirthankara—is located at Pavapuri. Pavapuri, situated in Nalanda district of Bihar, is a major pilgrimage site for Jains. Lord Mahavira gave up his body at Pavapuri in Bihar in 527 B. C., at the age of 72 years. In the given question, instead of “propounder of Jainism,” the wording “real propounder of Jainism” should be used, because as the propounder of Jainism, the name of Adinath or Rishabhdev is mentioned.

questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: The “14 Purvas” (Purva) are the earliest Jain texts. During the time of the last Nanda king, Sambhuta Vijay and Bhadrabahu were the heads of the Sangha. Bhadrabahu was the last person who knew the 14 Purvas given by Mahavira.

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.q: ‘Ajivaka’, sect was founded by:
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: Makkhali Gosala was initially a disciple of Mahavira, but later, due to differences, he gave up Mahavira’s discipleship. Various sources mention Ajivika teachers named Nandavachchha and Kissankichcha, who were active even before Makkhaliputta Gosala. This implies that the Ajivika sect existed even before Gosala. Probably, it was Gosala who made this sect popular. Therefore, by tradition, he came to be regarded as the propounder of the Ajivika sect.

questions.q: The place where Mahavira attained complete spiritual knowledge (Kaivalya) is -
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: After 12 years of severe penance and spiritual practice, Mahavira Swami attained Kaivalya (perfect knowledge) under a sal tree on the bank of the Rijupalika River near Jrimbhikagrama. As a result, he came to be known as a “Kevalin”.

questions.q: Who contributed the most to the development of the Bhagavata sect?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: The Bhagavata or Vaishnava religion reached its peak during the reign of the Gupta kings. The Gupta rulers were followers of Vaishnavism and probably adopted it as their state religion. Most rulers assumed the title “Paramabhagavata”. Garuda, the vehicle of Vishnu, was the royal emblem of the Guptas.

questions.q: Nathpanthis, Siddhas and Yogis made devotional religion popular in
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: The Nathpanthis, Siddhas and Yogis popularized the Bhakti religion in North India. Using simple reasoning and argument, they criticized the ritualistic practices of orthodox religion, other artificial aspects, and the social system of that time. They supported renunciation of the world. According to them, contemplation of the formless Supreme Truth and the experience of becoming one with it is the path to liberation. For this, they emphasized the need to give rigorous training to the mind and body through practices such as yogic postures, pranayama, and contemplation/meditation.

questions.q: The list of sixteen Mahajanapadas is available in –

questions.explanation: In the Buddhist text Anguttara Nikaya, a list of 16 Mahajanapadas is available. These are: (1) Anga, (2) Magadha, (3) Kashi, (4) Kosala, (5) Vajji, (6) Malla, (7) Chedi, (8) Vatsa, (9) Kuru, (10) Panchala, (11) Matsya, (12) Shurasena, (13) Ashmaka, (14) Avanti, (15) Gandhara, and (16) Kamboja. Among these, only Ashmaka was located in South India. In the Buddhist text Digha Nikaya, only 12 Mahajanapadas are mentioned. The Jain text Bhagavati Sutra also gives a list of 16 Mahajanapadas, but the names differ slightly there.

questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: The Nanda dynasty in Magadha was established after ending the Shishunaga dynasty. There were a total of 9 kings in the Nanda dynasty. In the later period of the Nandas, the people turned against the rulers due to forcible collection of money and heavy taxes even on small items, and an atmosphere of hatred and discontent spread everywhere. Taking advantage of this situation, Chandragupta Maurya, with the help of Chanakya, killed Dhanananda and ended the Nanda dynasty. Thus, immediately after the Nandas, the Maurya dynasty was established in Magadha. After that, the Shungas, Kanvas, Guptas, etc. ruled. Therefore, as per the question, the nearest correct answer is option (a).

questions.q: Which one of the following rulers of Magadha was the contemporary of Alexander, the Great?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: The last ruler of the Nanda dynasty was Dhanananda, who was a contemporary of Alexander. Greek writers called him Agrammes. Xenophon describes him as a very wealthy person. Bhaddasala was his commander-in-chief.

questions.q: Who recognized Sandrokottos as Chandragupta Maurya?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: William Jones was the first scholar who identified Sandrokottas (Sandrocottus) with the Mauryan ruler Chandragupta Maurya. Appian and Plutarch described Chandragupta Maurya as Androkottas/Androcottus, while Justin, Strabo, and Arrian mentioned him as Sandrokottas (Sandrocottus). Plutarch and Justin also mention the meeting between Chandragupta Maurya and Alexander the Great.

questions.q: The first empire was established by which ruler in India?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Chandragupta Maurya is counted among the great rulers of India. He was the first emperor of the Mauryan Empire. He was the first emperor who established his rule over a vast territory, and the extent of his empire was larger than the British Indian Empire. The boundary of his empire touched Iran. He was the first to politically unify India.

questions.q: Who was the founder of the Maurya Empire?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: The Maurya dynasty was founded by Chandragupta Maurya. Its period was 321–184 BCE. After this, the Kushana dynasty, the Gupta dynasty, and the Vardhana dynasty ruled ancient India.

questions.q: Who amongst the following Mauryan rulers did conquered the Deccan?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: Chandragupta Maurya, the founder of the Mauryan Empire, conquered South India (the Deccan). In this regard, information is obtained from Ashoka’s inscriptions, and from Jain and Tamil sources. Ashoka’s inscriptions are found at many places in the southern region, but Ashoka carried out only the Kalinga conquest. Therefore, the credit for conquest in the south has to be given to Chandragupta Maurya, because Bindusara’s conquests are highly doubtful and he is not remembered in history as a conqueror. Jain and Tamil sources also confirm Chandragupta Maurya’s southern conquest.

questions.q: Chandragupta Maurya figures prominently in the book of –
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: Detailed information about Chandragupta Maurya is obtained from Vishakhadatta’s 'Mudrarakshasa'. In this work, Chandragupta is considered the son of Mahapadma Nanda (another name—Nanda). In Mudrarakshasa, Chandragupta is also called “Vrishala” and “Kulheen.” In the 18th century CE, Dhundhiraj wrote a commentary on Mudrarakshasa.

questions.q: In how many categories did Megasthenes divide the Indian society?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: In his book Indica, Megasthenes divided Indian society into seven categories—(1) Philosophers, (2) Farmers, (3) Herders, (4) Craftsmen and businessmen, (5) Warriors, (6) Inspectors, and (7) Ministers and preachers. Megasthenes does not mention the prevalence of slavery in Indian society. In the Mauryan period, no person could marry outside his caste, nor could he adopt an occupation different from it.

questions.q: Which Chinese traveller visited India during Harshavardhana’s rule?

questions.explanation: The most important event of Harshavardhana’s time was the arrival of the Chinese traveller Hiuen Tsang in India. His strong desire was to see the places made sacred by the footprints of Gautama Buddha and to study the sacred Buddhist texts, which were available in India in those days. To fulfil this aim, he left Chang'an (Changan), the capital of the Tang rulers, for India in 629 CE. He wrote a book about his Indian journey, known as Si-Yu-Ki.

questions.q: Chinese traveller Hiuen Tsang studied at the University of –

He stayed at Nalanda for about 15 months and studied Yogashastra under Acharya Shilabhadra. After this, he reached Kanchi via Bengal, Odisha and Dhanyakataka. In the second phase of his journey, Hiuen Tsang again came to Nalanda in 642 CE. Thus, the total period of his stay at Nalanda (combining both visits) was about two years.

questions.q: During Hiuen-Tsang tour in India the most famous city for the production of cotton clothes was:

questions.q: In Indian art, the construction of ‘Stupa’, ‘Chaitya’ and ‘Vihara’ is related to which of the following?

A stupa is a place of worship, but it does not have a separate worship chamber. A chaitya is a prayer hall that includes a worship hall and a stupa; Buddhist monks used to sit in this hall and perform worship. A vihara is the residential monastery of Buddhist monks, used for study, rest and meditation.

Among these foreign writers, Megasthenes is the most important, and his book “Indica” is a major source for Mauryan history. In “Indica”, Megasthenes describes the municipal administration of Pataliputra. According to him, the administration of the city was carried out through committees comprising a total of 30 members. Those who evaded taxes were awarded the death penalty.
